transcript.text: Bosch integrated dishwasher showing E:15 and the pump keeps running. Model SMV4HTX31E. I've turned it off and on, still there

The E:15 code on your Bosch SMV4HTX31E means the anti-flood (water-protection) system has been triggered. This usually happens because there is an internal leak somewhere inside the dishwasher—commonly from the pump seals, sump hoses, or spray arm connections—that has dripped down into the base pan. It can also happen if water leaked from the door seal during a wash cycle. 1. Turn off the dishwasher at the mains (unplug it or switch off the isolation switch).
2. Pull the dishwasher out carefully so you can access the bottom.
3. Lay some old towels on the floor underneath the front edge of the machine.
4. Tilt the dishwasher back slightly (you may need two people for this) to see if any water drains out from under the base or front panel. Let me know if you find water in the base pan, and roughly how much. This will tell us if we are dealing with a confirmed internal leak that needs finding.

I can't pull it out or tilt it, it's integrated under the worktop and the plinth is glued at the ends. With a torch through a gap I can see a little shine of water in the base tray though. Anything else I can check from the front?

The shine in the base tray suggests water is sitting where it shouldn't be. Because you can't pull the machine out, we need to rule out the most common external causes from the front first. 1. Look closely at the rubber door seal all round the edge of the tub opening. Is it intact (no cuts or splits), and is there anything caught in it?
2. Open the dishwasher fully and spin both spray arms by hand. Do they rotate freely without catching on tall items or hitting the door seal? If either looks damaged or obstructed, that could be the source of a leak during washing. If both look fine, the leak is likely internal (pump seals or hoses), which will require an engineer to access safely.
Door seal looks okay, all round. I haven't checked the spray arms yet, will have a look. If they're fine, is it an engineer job then?

Yes. If the door seal is intact and the spray arms are not damaged or obstructed, the leak is probably internal—typically a weeping seal on the circulation pump or a cracked sump hose inside the base. Because your dishwasher is integrated with a glued plinth, accessing these parts requires removing the appliance from under the worktop and dismantling the base pan, which is beyond safe owner repair. Before you call an engineer, please check the spray arms as discussed:
1. Open the door and spin both spray arms by hand to ensure they rotate freely.
2. Look closely at the arms for cracks or splits, especially on the lower arm where water pressure is highest.
3. Ensure no tall items in the racks are deflecting the spray directly onto the door seal. If either arm is damaged or catching, replace the arm (this is a simple owner fix). If they look fine, you will need an engineer to locate and repair the internal leak.
